questions.question: Q: Two judges rank 5 contestants. The rank differences are: 0, 1, 1, 2, 0. Calculate Spearman's rₛ.
Q: Pearson's r for two variables is –0.85. Describe the correlation.
questions.correctAnswer: Strong negative linear correlation: as one variable increases, the other tends to decrease, and the points lie close to a straight line with negative slope.

questions.question: Q: A line of best fit is drawn for data where x ranges from 10 to 50. Is predicting y when x = 30 interpolation or extrapolation?
questions.correctAnswer: Interpolation, because x = 30 is within the observed range of 10 to 50.

questions.question: Q: Why is it unreliable to use a line of best fit to predict y when x = 90 if the observed x values range from 10 to 50?
questions.correctAnswer: This is extrapolation; we cannot assume the linear relationship continues beyond the observed data range.

questions.question: Q: Give a reason why correlation does not imply causation.
questions.correctAnswer: Two variables may be correlated due to a third confounding variable; e.g. ice cream sales and drowning rates are both linked to hot weather, not to each other.

questions.correctAnswer: Film | Rank 1 | Rank 2 | d (R1–R2) | d² A | 1 | 2 | –1 | 1 B | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 C | 3 | 4 | –1 | 1 D | 4 | 3 | 1 | 1 E | 5 | 6 | –1 | 1 F | 6 | 5 | 1 | 1 Σd² = 6 rₛ = 1 – 6Σd² ÷ (n(n² – 1)) = 1 – (6 × 6) ÷ (6 × 35) = 1 – 36 ÷ 210 = 1 – 0.171 = 0.829 rₛ ≈ 0.83, indicating strong positive agreement between the two judges. They rank the films in a very similar order.
